name: perf_sweep
result: batch 32=29s/10步, 64=57s/10步 -> 吞吐恒定271K tok/s (compute-bound); no_grad_ckpt NaN -> 根因见 850369a
hypothesis: Where is SFT throughput going, and why does disabling activation checkpointing produce NaN?
finding: Throughput is compute-bound at ~271K tok/s across 6 H20s — doubling the batch doubles step time exactly, so batch tuning is a dead end. The NaN has nothing to do with FP8 range (input amax 936 against an e4m3 limit of 448, scaling correct): Inductor's min-cut partitioner recomputes FP8LinearFunction's saved fp8 tensors in the backward graph, re-dividing already-scaled values. Isolated by bisection — eager is clean at batch 2 and 8 with Muon and 130 steps; adding torch.compile NaNs at step 1 with a finite forward and all 152 parameter gradients NaN.
decision: @torch._dynamo.disable on FP8Linear.forward (commit 850369a); verified 60 clean steps with compile on and grad_ckpt off. Activation checkpointing can now be dropped for roughly 25% more speed. Stop tuning batch size for throughput.

name: sft_v3
hypothesis: Does 489K verified rows from open Chinese datasets (Ape210K, Belle, Mxode, math23k) beat the baseline?
finding: No — 26.8%, a regression. Ape210K was 32% of the mix and its rows are a single line ('列式：5/3 = 1.667') with no intermediate steps. Average generation fell to 136 characters and the model started answering division with quotient-and-remainder where the gold answer is a fraction. A large share of one-line data actively destroys multi-step reasoning.
decision: Cap any single-line source at roughly 10% of the mix. Judge a math corpus by the step count of its solutions, not by its row count.

name: sft_v4
hypothesis: With Ape210K capped at 10% and openo1/s1k restored, does 2.4x the loss tokens of v3 beat the 32.2% baseline?
finding: Recovered the regression (32.0%) but did not beat the baseline, despite 175M loss tokens against v3's 72M. Three runs now sit within 0.2 points of 32%: this is a plateau, not noise. Generation is clean (132 chars, 89.6% boxed) and still arithmetically wrong. The corpus is also less diverse than its row count suggests — deduplication dropped 126K of Mxode's 220K rows as Belle prompts rewritten.
decision: Stop adding data drawn from the same distribution. Next: (a) the L3/L4 hard eval set, to establish whether 32% is a model ceiling or holdout saturation, since all 500 holdout problems come from Belle; (b) genuinely heterogeneous data — TinyGSM's 11.8M rows are MIT-licensed and share no distribution with Belle; (c) drop grad_ckpt now that the NaN cause is fixed, for ~25% faster iteration.

name: sft_v5
finding: Adding 76.7K program-generated rows (756 programs) on top of v4 changed nothing: 31.0% vs v4 32.0%, within noise. Four runs now sit at 31-32%. Also confirmed the FP8 NaN fix in production: grad_ckpt off ran 1150 steps with zero NaN at 393K tok/s vs 271K with it (+45%).
decision: Stop iterating on this holdout ��� it is saturated. Judge future runs on math_hard_eval_1k (same ckpt scores 0.8% there). Next levers are architecture (AttnRes from aupai-05) and genuinely out-of-distribution data (TinyGSM), not more same-distribution rows.

name: pretrain_k3_v2
hypothesis: Does the K3 hybrid (KDA + Gated MLA, hd=128) train stably in native FP8 at 206M?
finding: Yes — 2.26B tokens, 3 epochs, no NaN. FP8 e4m3 both directions is stable as long as activation checkpointing is on (root cause of that dependency found later, see perf_sweep).
decision: K3 becomes the base for every downstream stage; ckpt_k3-mla_2b_step2000.pt is the only valid pretrain checkpoint (the old ckpt.pt is a different architecture and will not load).

name: sft_stage1
hypothesis: What does the model score on Chinese grade-school math after a normal instruction SFT?
finding: 32.2% on the 500-problem holdout. The CoT is fluent and well-formed; the arithmetic inside it is wrong. Fluency and correctness are decoupled at this scale.
decision: Treat 32.2% as the number every later experiment must beat. Stop reading loss as progress — only holdout accuracy counts.

name: sft_math_stage2
hypothesis: Does a second SFT pass on math-only data lift math accuracy?
finding: No — 32.2%, unchanged. Stage-1 had already seen all of school_math, so stage-2 added no information, only more passes over the same rows.
decision: Stop doing stage-2 passes over data stage-1 already contains. New capability needs new data, not more epochs.

name: sft_short_stage2
hypothesis: Is the DeepSeek-style 'restate then rewrite' answer format what is holding accuracy back?
finding: No — 31.6%. The format did change (output halved in length, no second rewrite, boxed rate near 100%) but accuracy did not move. Format is a token-efficiency lever, not an accuracy lever.
decision: Keep the short format for cheaper generation and cleaner verification, but stop expecting accuracy from formatting work.

name: rlvr_stage2
hypothesis: Can GRPO with a verifiable boxed reward lift a 32% model?
finding: No — collapsed to 11.2%. Three causes, none of them the choice of RL algorithm: T=0.1 made the 8 samples per prompt near-identical so most groups had std=0 and zero advantage; there was no KL term or reference model, so 500 steps drifted unanchored; and at 32% pass@1 there was little gap between pass@1 and pass@8 for RL to amplify.
decision: No RL until SFT clears ~60% and pass@8 minus pass@1 is at least 15 points. When RL resumes: sequence-level ratio (GSPO), T around 0.8, KL beta 0.01-0.04, and only train on prompts with a 20-80% solve rate (the LFM-1.3B-Math selection rule).

name: sft_v2_stage1
hypothesis: Redo stage-1 from the pretrain checkpoint using only verified short-format data — better than the original mix?
finding: No — 26.4%. The rebuilt mix dropped openo1 (77K) and the full-length school_math_r1_zh (223K) in exchange for 110K filtered rows. Filtering raised per-row quality and lowered total information; accuracy followed the total, not the quality.
decision: Never let a quality filter shrink the corpus without replacing the volume. Verify aggressively, then backfill to at least the original token count.

name: sft_v5_hard
finding: The hard eval separates checkpoints that math-500 cannot: v4 scored 0.8% and v5 3.1% there, while on math-500 they are 32.0% vs 31.0% (indistinguishable). Absolute level is still near-zero — the model gets almost every arithmetic step wrong on L3/L4.
decision: math_hard_eval_1k is now the primary metric; math-500 is kept only as a regression tripwire.
